newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end lower as Wall St eyes rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end lower as Wall St eyes rate hike.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed lower on Tuesday in heavy trade, dragged by Wall Street on fears that the Fed would soon raise interest rates.
Dealers said volume was mainly accounted for by trading, with final investors largely expected to stay away from Spain until the budget is released.
The general index fell 1.44 points, 0.40 percent, to 358.38 and the Ibex fell 18.07 points, 0.44 percent, to 4,083.56.
Telefonica saw huge volume, with some profit-taking. The stock fell 25 pesetas to 2,390 with around seven million shares exchanged.
BBV bank bucked the trend, boosted by put-throughs. It added 60 pesetas to 5,610 backed by continued healthy broker sentiment.
Comments to Reuters by a senior Fed official that he saw a consensus for a 25 basis point rate hike in the Fed funds rate changed slim gains into losses.
"The news about the Fed prompted a rapid change in the market's trend after having absorbed some sales on profit-taking without any problems," said one dealer.
Volume was exceptionally heavy at around 49 billion pesetas.
